name: Part 91 Refresher
about: For certificated pilots staying current: the part 91 rules and the related part 61, 43 and 49 CFR 830 rules, AIM and ACs, with practice games. A good review before a flight review or IPC.

tasks.title: Flight Review and WINGS
tasks.objective: Know the flight review rule, what can take its place, and what a good review covers.

knowledge.text: Flight review requirements: ground and flight time, the 24 calendar month window, who may give it and the logbook endorsement.
What can take the place of a flight review: a practical test for a new certificate or rating, a phase of the FAA WINGS program, and other 61.56 exceptions.
What a flight review covers: a review of the current general operating and flight rules of part 91 and the maneuvers the instructor chooses.

risk_management.text: Treating the flight review as a box to tick every two years instead of a check on real proficiency.

skills.text: From a pilot's logbook, decide whether the flight review is current and when the next one is due.

tasks.title: Recent Flight Experience
tasks.objective: Know the recent flight experience rules to carry passengers, fly at night and fly IFR.

knowledge.text: Passenger-carrying currency: takeoffs and landings in the preceding 90 days, category, class and type, and full-stop landings in tailwheel airplanes.
Night currency: takeoffs and landings to a full stop during the period from 1 hour after sunset to 1 hour before sunrise.
Instrument currency: approaches, holding and course intercepting and tracking in 6 calendar months, the 6-month grace period and the instrument proficiency check.
Logging flight time and the experience used to meet currency, including safety pilot and simulated instrument time.

risk_management.text: Being current but not proficient after a long break.
Setting personal minimums that match recent experience.

skills.text: Given a logbook page, decide what the pilot may legally do today: carry passengers by day or night, or fly IFR.

tasks.title: Medical Certificates and BasicMed
tasks.objective: Know which medical you need, how long it lasts, BasicMed rules and when you must not fly.

knowledge.text: Medical certificate classes, which privileges each supports, and how long each lasts by age.
BasicMed: requirements (comprehensive medical examination checklist, online course, driver's license) and the aircraft and operating limits.
Medical deficiency: the 61.53 prohibition when you know or have reason to know of a condition or medication that makes you unable to meet the medical standards.

risk_management.text: Flying with a condition or medication that is not disqualifying on paper but makes you unsafe today.

skills.text: Decide whether a pilot with a given medical status may act as PIC on a given flight.

tasks.title: Pilot Documents and Required Notices
tasks.objective: Know what documents you must carry, show and report.

knowledge.text: Documents a pilot must have in physical possession or readily accessible when acting as PIC or a required crewmember, including photo identification.
Presenting your certificate and logbook when asked by the FAA, NTSB, TSA or law enforcement.
Required notices: change of permanent mailing address within 30 days and reporting motor vehicle actions involving alcohol or drugs within 60 days.

risk_management.text: Assuming an electronic copy or an old address is good enough.

skills.text: List the documents the pilot must have for a given flight and the notices the pilot owes the FAA.

tasks.title: Fitness for Flight: Alcohol, Drugs and Fatigue
tasks.objective: Know the alcohol and drug rules and how to judge whether you are fit to fly.

knowledge.text: Alcohol rules: 8 hours from bottle to throttle, the 0.04 blood alcohol limit, being under the influence, and testing.
Medications and drugs: effects of common over-the-counter medicines and the advice on waiting before flight.
Fatigue, stress and illness, and the IMSAFE personal checklist.

risk_management.text: Flying while legally allowed but impaired by fatigue, a hangover or medication.

skills.text: Use IMSAFE to decide whether a pilot is fit for a given flight.

tasks.title: Preflight Action and Fuel Requirements
tasks.objective: Know what the pilot in command must learn before every flight and the fuel rules for VFR and IFR.

knowledge.text: Pilot in command responsibility and authority.
Preflight action: weather reports and forecasts, fuel requirements, alternatives if the flight cannot be completed, known ATC delays, runway lengths, and takeoff and landing distance data.
VFR fuel requirements by day and night, and IFR fuel requirements.
Getting a complete preflight briefing and the information it contains.

risk_management.text: Leaving with only the legal minimum fuel.
Skipping the briefing on a familiar local flight.

skills.text: Plan the preflight action and fuel for a given flight.

tasks.title: Airworthiness and Required Aircraft Documents
tasks.objective: Know who is responsible for airworthiness and which documents must be on board.

knowledge.text: The PIC's responsibility to decide that the aircraft is airworthy, and the owner or operator's responsibility for maintaining it.
Documents required on board: airworthiness certificate, registration, operating limitations (flight manual, placards, markings) and weight and balance data.
Maintenance records the owner must keep and what they show.

risk_management.text: Flying an aircraft with an expired registration or missing documents.

skills.text: Inspect the documents of a given aircraft and decide whether it may fly.

tasks.title: Required Equipment and Inoperative Equipment
tasks.objective: Know the equipment needed for day VFR, night VFR and IFR, and how to handle equipment that doesn't work.

knowledge.text: Required instruments and equipment for day VFR, night VFR and IFR flight.
Flying with inoperative instruments or equipment without a minimum equipment list: the 91.213(d) steps.
Minimum equipment lists and letters of authorization.

risk_management.text: Flying with an inoperative item without deciding whether it is required or making the flight safe without it.

skills.text: Decide whether a given aircraft may fly with a given item inoperative, and what must be done first.

tasks.title: Inspections, Airworthiness Directives and Preventive Maintenance
tasks.objective: Know the inspections an aircraft needs, airworthiness directives and what an owner-pilot may do.

knowledge.text: Annual and 100-hour inspections and when each applies.
Other required checks: transponder, altimeter and static system, ELT, and VOR checks for IFR.
Airworthiness directives: what they are and how compliance is recorded.
Preventive maintenance a certificated pilot may do on an aircraft they own or operate, and the record entry required.

risk_management.text: Doing maintenance that isn't on the preventive maintenance list, or not recording it.

skills.text: From a set of aircraft records, find which inspections are due.

tasks.title: Airspace Classes and Equipment
tasks.objective: Know the entry, communication and equipment rules for each class of airspace.

knowledge.text: Class A, B, C, D, E and G airspace: dimensions and entry requirements.
Pilot certificate and communication requirements for each class.
Transponder and ADS-B Out requirements and where they apply.

risk_management.text: Entering Class B or C airspace without the required clearance or two-way communication.

skills.text: Plan a route through several classes of airspace and state what is needed for each.

tasks.title: VFR Weather Minimums, Special VFR and Cruising Altitudes
tasks.objective: Know the VFR visibility and cloud clearance rules, special VFR and VFR cruising altitudes.

knowledge.text: Basic VFR weather minimums by airspace class and altitude, day and night.
Operating within the surface area of controlled airspace: ceiling and visibility, and special VFR.
VFR cruising altitudes by magnetic course above 3,000 feet AGL.

risk_management.text: Continuing VFR into deteriorating weather.

skills.text: Decide whether a given VFR flight is legal at a given altitude and weather.

tasks.title: Special Use Airspace and Temporary Flight Restrictions
tasks.objective: Know the kinds of special use airspace and temporary flight restrictions and how to avoid violating them.

knowledge.text: Prohibited, restricted, warning, alert and military operations areas, and national security areas.
Temporary flight restrictions: kinds, how they are published as NOTAMs, and how to check them before flight.
The Washington, DC Special Flight Rules Area and other special rules airspace.

risk_management.text: Not checking NOTAMs for TFRs before every flight.

skills.text: Check a route for special use airspace and TFRs and plan around them.

tasks.title: Minimum Safe Altitudes and Speed Limits
tasks.objective: Know the minimum safe altitudes and aircraft speed limits.

knowledge.text: Minimum safe altitudes: anywhere, over congested areas, over other than congested areas, and over open water or sparsely populated areas.
Speed limits: below 10,000 feet MSL, near Class C and D airports, and under Class B airspace.

risk_management.text: Maneuvering low over people or property.

skills.text: Find the lowest legal altitude and highest legal speed at given points on a flight.

tasks.title: Right-of-Way and Collision Avoidance
tasks.objective: Know the right-of-way rules and how to see and avoid other aircraft.

knowledge.text: Right-of-way rules: aircraft in distress, converging, approaching head-on, overtaking and landing.
Operating near other aircraft and formation flight.
Collision avoidance: scanning, blind spots, lights, ADS-B In and traffic advisories.

risk_management.text: Relying on ATC or traffic displays instead of looking outside.

skills.text: Decide who has the right-of-way in given encounters and what each pilot should do.

tasks.title: Airport Operations, Light Signals and Runway Safety
tasks.objective: Know the rules at towered and non-towered airports and how to prevent runway incursions.

knowledge.text: Operating at non-towered airports: traffic pattern direction, recommended pattern entries and self-announce radio calls.
Operating at towered airports: clearances, taxi instructions, hold short instructions and ATC light gun signals.
Airport signs, markings and lighting, and runway incursion hot spots.

risk_management.text: Crossing a hold short line or entering a runway without clearance.

skills.text: Plan an arrival and departure at a non-towered airport and taxi at a towered airport.

tasks.title: ATC Clearances, Communications and Transponder Use
tasks.objective: Know when you must follow ATC, how to talk to ATC and how to use the transponder.

knowledge.text: Compliance with ATC clearances and instructions, and when a pilot may deviate.
Radio communication technique and phraseology.
Transponder codes, including 1200, 7500, 7600 and 7700, and when to squawk them.

risk_management.text: Accepting a clearance or instruction that would put the aircraft in danger.

skills.text: Respond to given ATC instructions and an equipment failure correctly.

tasks.title: Passengers, Seat Belts and Persons on Board
tasks.objective: Know your duties to passengers and the rules about seats, belts, devices and dropping objects.

knowledge.text: Passenger briefing on seat belts and shoulder harnesses, and when they must be fastened.
Careless or reckless operation, interference with crewmembers and dropping objects.
Portable electronic devices on board.

risk_management.text: Not briefing passengers on belts, doors, emergency exits and sterile cockpit.

skills.text: Give a complete passenger briefing for a given flight.

tasks.title: Supplemental Oxygen, Parachutes and Aerobatic Flight
tasks.objective: Know the oxygen rules and the rules for parachutes and aerobatic flight.

knowledge.text: Supplemental oxygen requirements for crew and passengers by cabin pressure altitude.
Hypoxia: types, symptoms and time of useful consciousness.
Where aerobatic flight is prohibited and when parachutes are required.

risk_management.text: Flying at high altitude without oxygen because you feel fine.

skills.text: Decide when oxygen must be used on a given flight.

tasks.title: IFR Flight Plans, Alternates and Fuel
tasks.objective: Know the IFR flight plan rules, when you need an alternate and the IFR fuel rule.

knowledge.text: When an IFR flight plan and clearance are required.
The alternate airport requirement and alternate airport weather minimums, including GPS-based alternates.
IFR fuel requirements.

risk_management.text: Choosing an alternate that is likely to have the same weather as the destination.

skills.text: Decide whether a given IFR flight needs an alternate and whether a given airport qualifies.

tasks.title: Takeoff, Approach and Landing Minimums
tasks.objective: Know the IFR takeoff, approach and landing rules.

knowledge.text: Takeoff minimums and obstacle departure procedures.
Descending below DA, DH or MDA: the required visual references and flight visibility.
Minimum altitudes for IFR operations.

risk_management.text: Descending below minimums without the required visual references.

skills.text: Decide at given points on an approach whether the pilot may continue or must go missed.

tasks.title: IFR Communications, Reports and Lost Communications
tasks.objective: Know the required IFR reports and what to do if the radios fail.

knowledge.text: Required reports to ATC under IFR.
Malfunction reports.
Two-way radio communications failure in VFR and IFR conditions: route, altitude, and leaving the clearance limit.

risk_management.text: Not knowing the lost communications plan before you need it.

skills.text: Apply the lost communications rules to a given flight.

tasks.title: IFR Equipment Checks and Databases
tasks.objective: Know the equipment checks and database currency needed for IFR.

knowledge.text: VOR receiver checks: kinds, limits and the record.
Altimeter, static system and transponder inspections for IFR.
GPS and navigation database currency and RAIM or integrity checks.

risk_management.text: Flying IFR with an expired navigation database without verifying the data.

skills.text: Decide whether a given aircraft is legal for an IFR flight.

tasks.title: Weather Decision-Making and Icing
tasks.objective: Use weather information to make sound go and no-go decisions, and avoid icing.

knowledge.text: Getting and using a complete weather briefing, including PIREPs and graphical products.
Structural icing: where to expect it, the hazards, and what the regulations allow in known icing.
Thunderstorm and low visibility hazards.

risk_management.text: Continued VFR into IMC.
Plan continuation bias.

skills.text: Make a go, no-go or divert decision for a given weather picture.

tasks.title: Loss of Control and Stall and Spin Awareness
tasks.objective: Recognize and prevent loss of control in flight.

knowledge.text: Angle of attack, stalls and what increases stall speed.
Situations that commonly lead to loss of control: base-to-final turns, go-arounds, departure climbs and distraction.
Stall and spin recovery.

risk_management.text: Maneuvering at low altitude with high bank and low airspeed.

skills.text: Explain the recovery from a given stall or upset.

tasks.title: Runway Safety: Incursions, Excursions and Overruns
tasks.objective: Prevent runway incursions and landing overruns.

knowledge.text: Single pilot procedures during taxi to prevent runway incursions.
Landing distance, contaminated runways and the stabilized approach.
When to go around.

risk_management.text: Pressing on with an unstable approach to a short or wet runway.

skills.text: Decide whether to land or go around in a given approach situation.

tasks.title: Technology in the Cockpit: EFBs, PEDs and Unfamiliar Aircraft
tasks.objective: Use electronic flight bags, portable devices and new avionics safely.

knowledge.text: Electronic flight bags: what they may replace and how to keep them working.
Portable electronic devices and interference.
Transitioning to an unfamiliar aircraft or avionics system.

risk_management.text: Over-reliance on automation and loss of situational awareness.

skills.text: Plan a transition to a new aircraft or avionics.

tasks.title: Emergency Authority and Getting Help
tasks.objective: Know your emergency authority and how to get help from ATC.

knowledge.text: The PIC's emergency authority to deviate from any rule, and the report ATC may request.
Declaring an emergency: distress and urgency calls, squawk 7700 and frequency 121.5.
Services available to pilots in an emergency.

risk_management.text: Waiting too long to declare an emergency.

skills.text: Handle a given emergency with ATC.

tasks.title: Accident and Incident Reporting (49 CFR 830)
tasks.objective: Know what must be reported to the NTSB, how fast, and how to preserve wreckage.

knowledge.text: Definitions of aircraft accident, serious injury, substantial damage and incident.
Incidents that require immediate notification.
Preserving wreckage and filing the written report.

risk_management.text: Not reporting an incident because no one was hurt.

skills.text: Decide whether a given event must be reported to the NTSB and how.

tasks.title: ELTs and Survival
tasks.objective: Know the ELT rules and how to be found and survive after an off-airport landing.

knowledge.text: ELT requirements, battery replacement and inspection.
Testing an ELT and what to do if one is activated by accident.
Survival planning: flight plans, equipment and what to do after an off-airport landing.

risk_management.text: Flying over remote terrain without a flight plan or survival gear.

skills.text: Plan survival equipment and search and rescue protection for a given flight.
